title: Password Strength
summary: Given a string password, calculate its strength by awarding 1 point for each distinct lowercase letter, 2 points for each distinct uppercase letter, 3 points for each distinct digit, and 5 points for each distinct special character from the set '!@#$', with each character contributing at most once.
statement: Given a string password, calculate its strength by awarding 1 point for each distinct lowercase letter, 2 points for each distinct uppercase letter, 3 points for each distinct digit, and 5 points for each distinct special character from the set '!@#$', with each character contributing at most once.
constraints: Each distinct lowercase letter is worth one, uppercase letter two, digit three, and character from !@#$ five.
Repeated copies of the same character contribute only once.
reference_solution:
def password_strength(password):
    return sum(1 if c.islower() else 2 if c.isupper() else 3 if c.isdigit() else 5 for c in set(password))
hints: Convert the password to a set so each character is visited once.
Classify each unique character by lowercase, uppercase, digit, or special.
Deduplication before classification enforces the at-most-once rule exactly.
editorial: Deduplication before classification enforces the at-most-once rule exactly.

tests.explanation: The four distinct character classes contribute 1+2+3+5=11.
Duplicates do not add points, so the same four unique characters still total eleven.
